prompts.question: What do you notice about the graph of (f(x)=x^3)?
prompts.answer: It is an odd function, its point of symmetry is at the origin, and its end behaviors are in opposite directions.

context.text: ADDITIONAL EXAMPLE 4 Determine the equation of the graph as it relates to the parent cubic function or parent quartic function. The graph has the shape of a cubic graph. prompts.question: How can you use the graph of (f(x)=(x-h)^3) to determine the value of (h)?
prompts.answer: Subtracting a number from (x) before cubing shifts the graph along the (x)-axis. By noting the direction that the graph of the function shifts, you can determine whether (h) is positive or negative. The magnitude of the shift will tell you the value of (h).

prompts.question: What do you notice about the graphs that can help you identify whether the function is even or odd?
prompts.answer: If the (y)-axis is an axis of symmetry of the graph, the function is even. If the origin is a point of symmetry of the graph, the function is odd.

prompts.question: When is it helpful to test points to determine whether a function is odd or even?
prompts.answer: Testing points is helpful if you cannot easily visually determine the symmetry of a graph.

prompts.answer: the symmetry of the graph; Evaluate (f(x)) and (f(-x)). If they are equal, then the function is even. Evaluate (f(-x)) and (-f(x)). If they are equal, then the function is odd.

prompts.question: If the highest degree of a function is even, why isn't that enough to say that it is an even function?
prompts.answer: By definition, an even function must have an axis of symmetry. Not all functions with an even degree have an axis of symmetry.

context.text: Use and Connect Mathematical Representations PART A

prompts.question: If the highest degree of a function is odd, why isn't that enough to say that it is an odd function?
prompts.answer: By definition, an odd function must have symmetry about the origin. Not all functions with an odd degree are symmetrical about the origin.

context.text: Use and Connect Mathematical Representations PART A

prompts.question: Compare and contrast the two functions shown in the graph.
prompts.answer: The graph of the parent function is wider. The graph of the transformed function is shifted below the (x)-axis. Both graphs are even, open upward, and are symmetrical across the (y)-axis.

context.text: Use and Connect Mathematical Representations PART A

prompts.question: Is the order in which you apply the transformations important?
prompts.answer: It doesn't matter in which order you apply the translations, but the vertical stretch should be applied before the vertical translation.

context.text: Use and Connect Mathematical Representations PART A

prompts.question: Why is knowing the graph of the parent function a valuable tool?
prompts.answer: Knowing the parent graph gives you a starting place. You do not have to make a table of points to graph the function; instead, you can compare the function to the parent function to determine the transformation.

context.text: Use and Connect Mathematical Representations PART A

prompts.question: How does the graph of a function (g(x)=a(x-h)^n+k) compare to the graph of the parent function (f(x)=x^n)?
prompts.answer: The (a)-value stretches or compresses the graph vertically, the (h)-value shifts the graph horizontally, and the (k)-value shifts the graph vertically.

prompts.question: If the graph were reflected across the (y)-axis, how would that change the equation of the function? What if it were reflected across the (x)-axis? Write the equations for both of these functions.
prompts.answer: If the graph were reflected across the (y)-axis, the equation would be (f(x)=-(x+6)^2+4). If the graph were reflected across the (x)-axis, the equation would be (f(x)=(x-6)^2-4).

prompts.question: What does it mean to scale the dimensions to any size?
prompts.answer: Each dimension will be multiplied by the same factor.

context.text: Pose Purposeful Questions

prompts.question: When finding the equation for a storage container that is 1 ft longer in every dimension, does it matter whether you replace (x) with (x+1) in the expression ((x)(x)(x-1)) or in the expression (x^3-x^2)?
prompts.answer: No, the two expressions are equivalent, so you will end up with the same answer no matter which expression you use. The calculations will be easier, though, if you use the first expression.
